::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 21st 1889  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Historical Society of Pennsylvania: Gratz Collection: Case 12, Box 4: Foreign Hymn Writers
:::

Dear [Sir](people/person_1074.qmd)

I send the quotation with another still more to the purpose- but I should not put in two ds- as certainly Hampshire always calls the plant cli-ders.[^1] However no doubt there is authority.

I was sorry to drop the[dictionary work](organizations/other_151.qmd) but occupations thickened on me so that I could not keep it up

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The OED entry for 'clithers' defined as 'Another name of  the plant clivers or cleavers' includes  illustrative  quotations from both *The Heir of Redclyffe* and *The Herb of the Field*, both referring to the plant as ‘cliders’.
